rationale: This is a functional-form swap (MUL→MIN) on an already-tested gen-3 signal whose two legs reduce, once the near-inert intangible-augmented denominator is stripped away, to the well-known gross-profitability × accruals pairing (Novy-Marx + Sloan), so it is more a cosmetic recombination of archive winners than a new mechanism.

A defensible incremental composite that keeps all legs on a bounded scale, but the pre-R&D-earnings and clean-accrual gates are mechanically correlated (both are functions of ib), so the third gate may add little beyond thinning the long leg — worth one test, not a strong prior.

The SUB-of-MINs construction genuinely cancels the intangible main effect and delivers an accrual spread scaled by intangible depth, making it the family's sharpest falsification test of whether the alpha is a true interaction rather than an R&D tilt plus a Sloan tilt; the earlier failed version used materially different inputs, so the retest is informative, though the signal is near-zero for most firms and will concentrate its bet in the tails.

Because MIN is not symmetric under negation (min(1−a,1−b)=1−max(a,b)), this genuinely isolates the "both-bad" corner rather than mirroring the archive's best long signal, the expected negative sign matches the expression's direction, and it plausibly converts the family's diffuse short-side alpha into cross-sectional evidence by replacing a fat-tailed signed z-score with bounded ranks.

It is close to a rediscovery of cash-based operating profitability (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev) with an R&D-capitalized denominator, and the stated rationale is internally wrong — gross profit (sale−cogs) never deducted R&D, so "adding R&D back" does not undo any expensing distortion but simply bolts an R&D-intensity tilt onto the numerator.

A clean single-lever diagnostic on the archive's best construct that would meaningfully distinguish within-industry mispricing from an unpriced sector tilt, though it is incremental by design and, if it works, mostly reinterprets rather than extends the existing result.
